name: Mrs. Mary Asare-Yeboah
summary: Financial management and corporate governance consultant with extensive banking, board and leadership experience.
profile: Mary Asare-Yeboah holds a BSc in Banking and Finance and an MBA in Finance from the University of Ghana; a Master of Arts in Ministry from Trinity Theological Seminary; and qualifications in psychology and guidance and counselling from Methodist University Ghana. She is a Fellow of IoD-Gh and the Chartered Institute of Bankers Ghana, a Licensed Insolvency Practitioner and a Professional Counsellor licensed by the Ghana Psychology Council.

She began her career as an Administrative Manager with Shell Ghana Limited, before joining HFC, now Republic Bank, where she led departments and established new businesses for the bank. She is a Consultant in Financial Management and Corporate Governance, an IFC-trained Trainer of Trainers in ESG, and a director for corporate organisations.

Mary was elected to the IoD-Gh Council in 2021 and became Vice President in 2023. Following the premature exit of the former CEO in 2024, she chaired the Interim Management Committee, which ensured seamless management of the Institute's Secretariat. She was elected President in June 2025 and invested on 4 July 2025.

name: Mr. Michael Justice Ashong
summary: Executive and board leader with almost three decades of multi-sector corporate experience across Africa.
profile: Michael Ashong is Vice President of the 11th Governing Council of IoD-Gh. With almost three decades of executive and board-level experience in multi-sector corporates across Africa, he brings strategic leadership, governance insight and financial acumen to the Institute.

As a Fellow and member of the previous IoD-Gh Council, he chaired five key committees, including Strategy, Audit, ESG Training and the 25th Anniversary Committee. His investment banking background informs his work in problem-solving, communication and stakeholder engagement.

He commenced his career at UMB and later joined Ecobank, where he established and managed Ecobank Development Corporation in several countries. He holds Executive MBA and BSc degrees from the University of Ghana, professional certificates from The New York Institute of Finance and has served on boards in Ghana and across Africa.

name: Mr. Ekow Peterson Afedzie
summary: Former Managing Director of the Ghana Stock Exchange with more than two decades of board experience.
profile: Mr. Afedzie is a Fellow of IoD-Gh and was a member of the 10th Council from 2023 to 2025, serving on the Governance, Legal and Ethics Committee and the Risk Committee.

He is the former Managing Director of the Ghana Stock Exchange and a former member of its Council. He worked with the Exchange from its establishment in 1990 for more than 32 years, coordinated the establishment of the Ghana Fixed Income Market and Ghana Alternative Market, and has over 20 years of board experience.

He holds MBA and MA degrees from the University of Ghana, a BSc in Agriculture, an LLB from Mountcrest University College and a Qualifying Certificate in Law from the Ghana School of Law. He is a member of the Ghana Bar Association and the Chartered Institute of Marketing Ghana.

name: Mr. Kofi Okofo Dartey
summary: Management, finance, strategy and auditing professional with more than 30 years of experience.
profile: Mr. Okofo Dartey holds an MBA in Finance from the University of Ghana, a Bachelor of Commerce degree and a Diploma in Education from the University of Cape Coast. He is a Fellow of IoD-Gh and has served on its SME Mentorship and Audit Committees.

He is also a Fellow of the Institute of Chartered Accountants Ghana, a founding member of the Institute of Internal Auditors Ghana and a member of the Institute of Internal Auditors, Florida. He has more than 30 years of experience across the private and public sectors.

He is Managing Consultant at Okodart Consult, providing management and financial advisory services. He was a member of the Transitional Management Team that operationalised Ghana Grid Company Limited and has served on Audit Committees of various public institutions.

name: Mr. Sulemanu Koney
summary: Mining-sector leader recognised for advancing sustainable and inclusive growth across Ghana and ECOWAS.
profile: Mr. Sulemanu Koney is a distinguished leader in Ghana and the ECOWAS mining sector. As former CEO of the Ghana Chamber of Mines, he championed sustainable mining and fostered partnerships between multinationals and government.
He holds a BSc in Chemical Engineering from KNUST, an MSc in International Business from Maastricht, a postgraduate diploma in marketing from CIM-UK and an honorary doctorate from UMaT.

His board engagements include UMaT, GHEITI, the National Petroleum Authority, CSIR and the ECOWAS Federation of Chambers of Mines. He is Immediate Past Chair of the Global Compact Network Ghana and a Fellow of both IoD-Gh and CIM-UK.

name: Mr. Herbert Lawson
summary: Business banker and adviser with experience across engineering, real estate, finance and marketing.
profile: Mr. Lawson is a business banker with experience in engineering, real estate, finance, marketing and business advisory. He holds an Engineering Degree from KNUST, a postgraduate diploma in Marketing from the University of Roehampton, an MBA from the University of South Wales and is pursuing a PhD in Business Administration.

He is an associate member of the Chartered Institute of Marketing Ghana and a module reviewer for the Chartered Institute of Securities and Investments, UK. He works with the Business Development team at Guaranty Trust Bank Ghana PLC after previous senior management roles at First Atlantic Bank PLC and SG Bank PLC.
As a member of the 10th IoD-Gh Governing Council, he served on several Council Committees supporting the Institute's role in director development and corporate governance.

name: Dr. Rejoice Wodomdedzi Foli
summary: Corporate risk and governance consultant, project management adviser and licensed psychologist.
profile: Dr. Rejoice Wodomdedzi Foli is a UN Global Peace Ambassador and Special Envoy to Ghana for WOLMI-I.C.C, a UN-accredited agency. She is a Corporate Risk and Governance Consultant, Project Management Adviser and Licensed Psychologist, and advocates for ESG and SDG initiatives.

At IoD-Gh, she served on the 10th Council from 2023 to 2025, as Secretary of the Risk Committee and a member of the Governance, Legal and Ethics Committee. She has also served on the Regional Outreach, Educational Capacity Development and Research, and SME Mentorship committees, and was Project Manager for the development of Ghana's National Corporate Governance Code in 2022.
Her leadership includes board roles with WILDAF and the Street Children Empowerment Foundation, and project-director experience in UN, AU and EU sustainable community development initiatives.

name: Apostle (Dr.) Christopher Kwame Sokpor
summary: Chartered accountant, economist and governance professional with more than 20 years of experience.
profile: Apostle Dr. Christopher Kwame Sokpor holds a PhD in Accounting from Capella University, USA. He is a Chartered Accountant, Economist, Tax Practitioner and corporate governance professional with more than 20 years of expertise.

He is Founder and Senior Partner at Deon and Noed International, where he leads audit, tax, advisory and HR consulting in multiple countries. Previously, he worked with KPMG, World Bank projects and more than 25 multi-donor funded projects.

His governance experience includes board service with the Public Interest and Accountability Committee, Leverage Counselling Network and the College of Counselling and Psychology. He brings a commitment to accountability, transparency and institutional development.

name: Mr. Robert O. Mensah
summary: Business leader with 20 years of strategic and commercial leadership experience.
profile: Robert Mensah is a business leader with 20 years of strategic and commercial leadership experience. As General Manager of Eusbett Hotel, he led its transformation from a 16-room, two-star facility into a 250-room, four-star hotel with 200 employees and Ghana's largest conference centre.

In 2024, he was named CIMG Marketing Practitioner of the Year, the first hotelier and non-Accra-based recipient. He was also recognised as Up and Coming Director of the Year in 2019 by IoD-Gh. He holds an MBA in Finance and is a member of several professional bodies.

He has been a founding Regional Executive Committee Member of IoD-Gh for the Bono, Bono East and Ahafo Regions since June 2019. He served on the 10th Governing Council and chaired both the Risk Committee and the Governance, Legal and Ethics Committee.

name: Mrs. Emma Nancy Mullen-Essien
summary: Lawyer and board-governance specialist with more than 15 years of legal-sector experience.
profile: Emma Mullen-Essien is a lawyer with more than 15 years of experience across legal sectors, with expertise in board management, legal services, corporate protection, compliance, negotiation and advocacy.

She is Deputy Head of Legal at the Ghana Export-Import Bank, providing legal advice and support to the Board, Executive Management and departments. She previously served as Company Secretary and as Senior Legal Officer and Manager of the Board Secretariat at the erstwhile EDAIF.

Emma holds an LLM from Robert Gordon University, a Professional Certificate for Law Practice in Ghana, an EMBA from the University of Ghana Business School, and LLB and BA degrees from the University of Ghana. She is a member of the Ghana Bar Association, International Bar Association and Chartered Institute of Arbitrators, UK.
